title: Double Before the Ending
kidRule: When a short word ends with one short vowel and then one consonant, double that last consonant before adding ING, ED, ER or EST: plan becomes planning. Longer words do it too when their last beat is the strong one: forgot becomes forgotten. The letters W, X and Y never double (snowing, mixing, playing).
hint: Listen to the vowel in the small word: is it short and quick? Then look closely at the letter just before the ending.
reminder: After one short vowel, double the last consonant before you add I-N-G, E-D, E-R or E-S-T.

check.question: Why does PLANNING have two N's?
check.correctAnswer: PLAN has a short vowel and then one consonant, so we double the N before adding ING!
distractors: Because every word that ends in ING needs a double letter
Because it is a long word, and long words get extra letters

words.why: SWIM doubles its M before E-R is added.
words.def: Someone who moves through water using their arms and legs.
words.sent: My sister is a strong swimmer.
words.story: An elephant is a great swimmer and can use its trunk like a snorkel!
words.card: The *swimmer* taught a duck to *swim* backward!

words.why: PLAN doubles its N before I-N-G is added.
words.def: Working out ahead of time how you will do something.
words.sent: We are planning a surprise party for Dad.
words.story: Squirrels act as if they are planning ahead: in the fall they bury nuts to eat during the winter!
words.card: The ants are *planning* a clever *plan* to carry off the whole picnic!

words.why: BIG doubles its G before E-S-T is added.
words.sent: I picked the biggest pumpkin in the patch.
words.story: The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived, even bigger than the dinosaurs!
words.card: The *big* pig sat on the *biggest* fig!

words.why: GRAB doubles its B before E-D is added.
words.sent: The monkey grabbed a banana and ran.
words.story: A chameleon's tongue shoots out so fast that it has grabbed a bug before you can blink!
words.card: The crab *grabbed* my blanket and went to *bed*!

words.why: SHRUG doubles its G before E-D is added.
words.def: Lifted your shoulders up and down to show you do not know or do not mind.
words.sent: He shrugged when I asked where the cookies went.
words.story: In many countries around the world, lifting your shoulders is understood to mean 'I don't know'!
words.card: The caterpillar *shrugged* and rolled itself up in the *rug*!

words.why: FORGOT doubles its T before E-N is added.
words.sent: I have forgotten where I put my mittens.
words.story: Squirrels bury thousands of nuts, and the forgotten ones can sprout into new trees!
words.card: The elephant *got* to the party but had *forgotten* its trunk full of presents!

words.why: ADMIT doubles its T before E-D is added.
words.def: Said that something was true, even though it was hard to say.
words.sent: My brother admitted that he ate the last cookie.
words.story: A famous story says young George Washington admitted to chopping his father's cherry tree, but the tale was made up by a writer after Washington died!
words.card: The catcher *admitted* that he hid a sandwich in his *mitt*!

words.why: REGRET doubles its T before E-D is added.
words.def: Felt sorry about something you did.
words.sent: She regretted eating three slices of cake.
words.story: When a dog looks sorry, scientists found it is mostly reacting to its owner's scolding voice, whether or not it did anything wrong!
words.card: The *egret* *regretted* standing on one leg in the wet cement!

words.why: BEGIN doubles its N before I-N-G is added.
words.def: The very first part of something.
words.sent: The beginning of the movie was very funny.
words.story: Many fairy tales have the same four words at the beginning: 'Once upon a time'!
words.card: At the *beginning* of the trip, a goat checked into the *inn*!

words.why: EQUIP doubles its P before E-D is added.
words.def: Given all the tools or gear needed for a job.
words.sent: The fire truck is equipped with a very long ladder.
words.story: A spacesuit is equipped with its own supply of air, and even a drink bag with a straw inside the helmet!
words.card: The clown was *equipped* with a funny *quip* and a rubber chicken!
